item.title: Canopy 0.3.0
item.description:
Added

  • Saved scans and fast rescans: every scan is kept on disk, and a rescan reads only the folders that changed since then (via the macOS file system event history) instead of the whole tree.
  • Live view while scanning: the largest top-level folders grow on screen as the scan runs.
  • Cleanup basket: collect files and folders from anywhere in the app, review them and move them to the Trash in one confirmed step. System and app-critical locations are protected and cannot be added.
  • Space hogs: a Cleanup sheet finds typical space wasters (app caches, developer build output and simulators, device backups, Docker data, old downloads, large files untouched for a year) and adds them to the basket.
  • Duplicate finder: finds identical files, accounts for APFS clones when showing reclaimable space, and never moves the last copy to the Trash.
  • History and comparison: each scan leaves a summary, and "what grew" compares a folder with an earlier scan.
  • Interactive charts: the file-type donut shows details on hover, a legend and "Where are these files?".
  • Reports: export a summary, folder list, largest files, cleanup or changes report as PDF or CSV, in German or English, with optional company branding.
  • Menu bar item: free space of your disks with a low-space warning and your most recent scans; Canopy keeps running there after its last window closes (can be turned off in Settings).
  • Finder integration: drop folders onto the window or the Dock icon, open folders with "Open With" > Canopy, Quick Look with the space bar.
  • Explorer search (name and path, ⌘F), sorting by size, name or last modified, filters for minimum size and cloud placeholders, and a context menu with Show in Finder, Open, Copy Path and Scan This Folder.
  • Command line: Canopy scan, top, history, compare, report and bench run without opening the app; Canopy --version prints version, build and commit.
  • The About window, Settings and Canopy --version show version, build number and commit.
  • Automatic updates: "Check for Updates…" in the Canopy menu and the menu bar item, and an Updates section in Settings (automatic checks on/off, check now, last check). Canopy asks once before checking automatically and shows the release notes before installing.

Changed

  • Much faster scanning: a new parallel scan engine reads folders on all cores with a single system call per batch of entries.
  • Sizes show the space actually used on disk as the main value everywhere (sparse files and clones no longer inflate totals); files with sparse data are marked.
  • Online-only OneDrive and iCloud folders are marked instead of downloaded while scanning, so scans of cloud storage finish in seconds. A full cloud scan is available per folder and as a setting.
  • Scan progress updates at least every 250 ms, also in slow cloud folders.

Fixed

  • Scans no longer hang while a macOS privacy prompt (Desktop, Documents, other apps' data, ...) waits for an answer: a folder that makes no progress for 10 s is counted as unreadable, the scan finishes, and the next rescan reads the folder again.
  • Running scans can be stopped (sidebar button, Stop Scan, ⌘.), and stopping now actually reaches the scanner.
  • Hard-linked files are counted once, always in the same folder, so totals are stable between scans.
  • A failed background rescan keeps the last result and marks it as outdated instead of showing an error.
  • Fixed a hang at launch caused by the menu bar item and a crash in the file-type chart.
  • Fixed report fraction conversion for Swift 6 toolchains.
